newsitem.title: USA: Minn. lawmakers pass $6.7 bln school funding plan.
newsitem.headline: Minn. lawmakers pass $6.7 bln school funding plan.

text.p: Minnesota legislators have approved a two-year $6.7 billion education funding plan that resolves a dispute over tuition credits, a spokesman for Gov. Arne Carlson said Friday.
Lawmakers concluded a one-day special session Thursday evening that resolved the last of the issues remaining for Minnesota's fiscal biennium beginning Tuesday, spokesman Brian Dietz said.
Carlson is expected to receive the spending plan Friday and is likely to sign it on Monday, Dietz said.
Carlson had vetoed the entire elementary and secondary education funding package earlier in June because it lacked $150 million of tax credits he had proposed that included private school tuitions.
After lengthy negotiations, Carlson, House Speaker Phil Carruthers, Senate Majority Leader Roger Moe and House Minority Leader Steve Sviggum announced a compromise on Wednesday.
The compromise adds $75 million of credits annually provided that revenue forecasts in November show that funding is available.
The plan allows education tax deductions for computer software and hardware, tutoring and education summer camps.
The plan also expands working family credits and introduces a refundable education tax credit for families with incomes of $33,500 or less beginning in the 1998 tax year.
The new refundable credit would provide $1,000 per child and up to $2,000 per family and applies to all items under the tax deduction except tuition for private schools.
